messages:
mike: Heads up — noticed a ~15% throughput regression on some A100 nodes for seq_len=4096 after yesterday's kernel-routing change. Logs show we picked a generic f32 attention kernel instead of the tensor-core bf16 path.
anya: ugh, do you have the perf trace? which nodes/SM versions?
mike: Attached snippet from runtime profiler: 
```
selected_kernel: attention_f32
seq_len: 4096
sm: 80
throughput_tokens_per_s: 1020
expected_kernel: attn_bf16_tc
expected_throughput: ~1200
```
this is on a mixed pool: some are SM 80, others 90. It looks like our capability detection returned a conservative set for a subset of nodes.
lina: I saw this on Friday—some machines report CUDA driver/ABI mismatch during cold probe, falling back to conservative flags. We already have /etc/redwood/gpu_cap_flags.json on the node, but the startup probe sometimes races with driver module loading.
raj: Quick diag: can you run on one of the affected nodes: `python -c "import torch,os;print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))"` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv`? Also check `cudaDeviceGetAttribute` for `cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor`/Minor. If those are 8/0 or 8/6 we should enable BF16 tensor-core kernels.
mike: ran those: 
```
Device name: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
compute capability: 8.0
nvidia-smi compute_cap: 8.0
runtime-probe: reported_cap_flags: {"bf16_tc": false, "fp8": false}
```
so the hw advertises 8.0 but our probe flipped flags to false.
eva: I think the problem is the new seq_len routing logic: for seq_len > 2048 we route to long_seq_path which expects kv_prefetch + tc kernels. But kv_prefetch is only toggled when cap_flags.bf16_tc == true. Because the probe said false, we took a slower path and missed batched KV prefetch. That explains extra copies and lower throughput.
anya: any quick mitigation while we fix probe? Can we allow an override per-pool?
lina: yes — we have env override support via REDWOOD_GPU_OVERRIDES in the systemd unit but it's not exposed in autoscaler. We can push a canary that sets `REDWOOD_GPU_OVERRIDES="bf16_tc=true,fp8=false"` for the affected pool.
raj: Long-term fix: change probe to use a two-step detection: first read driver/device attributes (compute capability), then validate by launching a tiny bf16 tc microkernel (one-shot run) to ensure the runtime actually supports it. If microkernel fails, fall back. This avoids false negatives from early driver race. Pseudocode: 
```
int major, minor; cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&major, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, 0); // ...minor
if (major>=8) {
  if (run_bf16_tc_probe()) cap_flags.bf16_tc = true;
}
```
eva: Also add a short timeout + retry for probe at startup and mark node status as 'probing' so autoscaler doesn't route heavy long-seq traffic until probe completes.
perf-bot: Canary metrics: before override: 1020 tok/s (p95 latency 110ms). After manual override on pool-3: 1195 tok/s (p95 85ms).
mike: sweet — let's roll the override for pool-3 now and queue the probe fix PR. I'll open a short-lived feature flag to gate the microkernel check.
anya: please include test in eng-ml infra harness that simulates driver-init delay so we don't regress again.
lina: noted. I'll draft PR: runtime: add microkernel probe + retry + env override support for pool-level flags.
raj: will review. Also adding a small perf test for seq_len=4096 and seq_len=8192 to catch path selection regressions in CI.
mike: thanks all — rolling canary and creating incident ticket to track until PR lands. :thumbsup:
